cf.title: Assertion failure in WAL summarizer after promotion

verdict_reasoning: No surviving objection questions the goal or the design. The series fixes a reproduced assertion failure and a silent wrong restore from incremental backup. The two surviving objections are fixable: maintenance-fit-1 asks for a branch plan for 0002 and 0003, and replication-ondisk-1 asks how a user recovers after 0002 refuses a backup. Both are decisions for a committer who knows the summarizer and backpatch policy.

brief.title: Fix WAL summarizer assertion and incremental backup loss after promotion
brief.problem: After a standby paused at a recovery target is promoted, the WAL summarizer, which has summarized past the target, fails Assert("end_of_summary_lsn >= current_lsn") and the postmaster restarts the cluster. The same root cause lets a timeline 1 summary cover WAL past the switch point, so an incremental backup on the promoted server can skip changed blocks and restore old data without error. This affects users of summarize_wal and incremental backup since 17.
brief.proposed_design: The v4 series has three patches. 0001 makes SummarizeWAL() report no progress when read_upto moved back before the summary start, so the main loop rewinds to the switch point. 0002 makes incremental backup refuse a truncation recorded in a summary that crosses a timeline switch point, and 0003 makes GetLatestLSN() return the replay position during recovery, so standbys never summarize past replay.
user_visible_surface: An incremental backup now fails when an existing WAL summary records a truncation and crosses a timeline switch point (0002).
On a standby the WAL summarizer now stops at the replay position instead of the walreceiver flush position, so pg_available_wal_summaries() shows less WAL there (0003).
author_claims: The assertion failure goes back to 17 and v1/v2 of the fix apply to master, 19, 18 and 17.
Builds without assertions recover from the assertion case on their own, with the same summaries and state as with 0001.
Shihao's test restores a table with 4|0 instead of 4|1 on master without cassert (3 of 3 runs) and passes with the series.
0003 alone does not fix summaries already on disk, so 0002 refuses them, because summary entries carry no LSNs.
Robert Haas states that nothing relies on standby summaries ahead of replay.
brief.thread_state: Fujii reported the bug; Daria and Sai Pranav confirmed it and tested, Robert answered the 0003 question, and Sai Pranav gave LGTM on v4. Open: 0003 commit message names stale test file names, and no committer has said whether the series goes in or how far it is backpatched.
unclear: The material does not say whether 0002 and 0003 are meant to be backpatched like 0001, or only applied to master.
The material does not say what error message or hint a user sees when 0002 refuses a backup, or how the user recovers.
Message #8 says Fujii committed something that v3 sits on, but the material does not say what that commit contains.
The material does not say whether limiting summarization to replay delays incremental backups taken from a lagging standby.

objections.title: Backpatch scope for the data-loss fixes 0002 and 0003 is not stated
objections.failure_scenario: A committer pushes 0001 with its Backpatch-through: 17 tag and leaves 0002 and 0003 on master only. A user on 17 promotes a standby that was paused at a recovery target and later takes an incremental backup. That backup restores old table data without any error, and the user finds out only when the restored data is wrong.
objections.argument: Only v1-0001 carries a Backpatch-through line. Message #2 says 0001 applies to 17-19, but messages #6 and #8 put the silent data loss in 0002 and 0003, and they say nothing about branches. If 0003 is backpatched, standbys on stable branches change behavior, because pg_available_wal_summaries() shows less WAL there. A committer would likely ask for the branch plan for each patch before taking ownership of all three.
objections.author_must_show: Which of 0002 and 0003 are meant for 17, 18 and 19, and what does a user on those branches see when 0002 refuses a backup?

critic.reasoning: Only 0001 carries a Backpatch-through line, while messages #5 and #6 tie the silent data loss to the 0002 and 0003 fixes. No message gives a branch plan for those two, and 0003 changes standby behavior if backpatched.

objections.title: 0002 refusal gives users no stated way back to working incremental backups
objections.failure_scenario: A user promoted a standby on 17 and the old timeline summary on disk crosses the switch point and records a truncation. After a minor update with 0002, every scheduled incremental backup fails. The proposal does not say whether the user must take a new full backup, delete summary files, or wait.
objections.argument: 0002 exists because bad summaries already on disk cannot be repaired: entries carry no LSNs (message #6). That on-disk state persists after the fix, so the refusal can repeat on every backup. The material shows no error text, hint, or documented remedy, and it does not say whether 0002 is backpatched with 0001. A committer would likely ask for both before shipping a new hard failure in back branches.
objections.author_must_show: What error and hint does a user see when 0002 refuses, does a new full backup clear the condition, and is 0002 meant for back branches?

critic.reasoning: Message #6 confirms 0002 refuses summaries already on disk, and the thread does not say how a user gets back to working incremental backups. A new full backup probably clears the condition, but the proposal does not say so.

refuted.title: Refused incremental backup has no stated message or recovery path
refuted.failure_scenario: An operator runs nightly incremental backups from a server promoted after a recovery-target pause. After a minor upgrade that includes 0002, the job starts failing. Nothing in the proposal says whether the error tells the operator to take a new full backup, so the operator may retry or open a support case before learning the incremental chain is unusable.
refuted.argument: 0002 turns a silent wrong result into a hard failure, which is the right direction. It does this for summaries already on disk (message #6), so existing users can hit it right after an upgrade. The patch prose shows no documentation hunk, no error text and no hint. The material also does not say whether 0002 and 0003 carry Backpatch-through: 17 like 0001. That decides whether this new failure shows up in a minor release.
refuted.author_must_show: What error and hint does 0002 report, what must the user do to recover, and will 0002 and 0003 be backpatched to 17?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-1, which states the recovery question more precisely. Its claim that the patch prose shows no error text is weak, because the material includes prose only for v1-0001 and none for 0002.

touch_points.label: on-disk format / pg_upgrade
touch_points.reason: 0002 refuses WAL summary files already on disk that record a truncation and cross a timeline switch point.

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: 0003 makes the standby WAL summarizer stop at the replay position, and 0001 changes its behavior after promotion.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: 0001 is tagged Backpatch-through: 17, and the thread gives no branch plan for 0002 and 0003.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: 0002 adds a refusal path in incremental backup that must stay while old summaries can exist.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Which of 0002 and 0003 are meant for 17, 18 and 19, and which only for master?
What error message and hint does a user see when 0002 refuses an incremental backup?
Does a new full backup clear the 0002 refusal, or must the user also remove old summary files?
Does stopping summarization at the replay position delay or block incremental backups taken from a lagging standby?
Which commit does v3 build on, and do the back branches need it before 0002 and 0003 apply?

committability.owner_note: Someone who knows the WAL summarizer and incremental backup code must sign. Fujii Masao reported the bug and Robert Haas answered the 0003 question, but neither has said whether the series goes in.
committability.liability: The owner signs for incremental backup correctness across timeline switches in every branch that gets the fix. If 0002 and 0003 are backpatched, the owner also signs for a new backup refusal and changed standby summarization in minor releases.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted four versions in about three weeks and answered review comments, which suggests the author stays for fixes.

priority.reason: The series fixes a silent wrong restore for users of summarize_wal and incremental backup who promote a standby, and it adds no new user-facing setting or format. Review cost is medium because no code was read and the three patches touch the summarizer and incremental backup.

provisional_note: Only the v1-0001 prose and 3 of 13 messages were read. The 0002 check, its error text, and whether 0003 changes other callers of GetLatestLSN() could not be judged without the code.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_buffercache: Add per-relation summary stats
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a function to pg_buffercache, first pg_buffercache_relation_stats() and later renamed pg_buffercache_relations(), that scans shared buffers once. It returns per-relfilenode and per-fork counts of buffers, dirty buffers, pinned buffers and average usage count, aggregated in a hash table so a query does not need a tuplestore row for every buffer.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Ashutosh Bapat did not want more hand-aggregation functions: they copy what hash aggregates already do and add maintenance cost, for example for testing resizable shared buffers. Reviewers also noted that the in-function hash table does not respect work_mem or spill to disk. The author stopped posting new versions until the work_mem problem was solved, citing unclear interest. The thread then moved to a separate pg_buffercache_pages() tuplestore patch, which was committed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I'll hold off on posting a new version for now, since I think we'd have to figure out a solution to the work_mem question at the very least, and it sounds like right now its also a toss-up in terms of overall interest to get this committed.

precedents_retrieved.title: Summary Sort workers Stats in EXPLAIN ANALYZE
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes EXPLAIN ANALYZE so that Sort node statistics from parallel workers are summarized (average and peak sort space used, sort method, number of workers) instead of being printed per worker. This follows the approach already used by show_incremental_sort_group_info() and is meant to reduce output size when many workers are used.
precedents_retrieved.objection: After a review pointing out issues (summary only in non-VERBOSE mode, reporting workers planned rather than launched, unclear text format), the author posted a revised patch, but the patch later failed regression tests on all platforms. A reviewer asked for an updated patch, none was posted, and the entry was marked Returned with Feedback for lack of an update.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: This has been marked as RwF based on the lack of an update.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add timeline to partial WAL segments
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds the timeline that a promoted server switches to into the name of the .partial WAL segment it archives, for example 000000010000000100000001.00000002.partial. This prevents archive conflicts when several promotions in HA setups produce the same .partial file; prioritizing .history files in the archiver was proposed alongside it.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author stopped working on it. After discussion, Michael Paquier agreed with a revised scheme in which pg_receivewal would also use the timeline-suffixed name. The author then marked the patch Waiting on Author because it needed more work, and no new version followed for about 20 months. Robert Haas and Michael Paquier also objected to back-patching the naming change into minor releases, but that did not decide the entry.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: As nothing has happened here, I have marked the patch as RwF.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow PostgreSQL to perform promote/pause/shutdown operations at end-of-the-wal when the recovery does not reach the recovery target
precedents_retrieved.summary: The proposal stops recovery from promoting at the end of available WAL when the recovery target was not reached, with a new setting (recovery_target_incomplete) to promote, pause or shut down instead. It later split into a second patch that refuses to start WAL replay when the recovery target lies before the restored backup's position, checked against pg_control.
precedents_retrieved.objection: David Steele found the start-point check incorrect: it uses the checkpoint in pg_control, but backup recovery starts from the backup_label checkpoint, and PITR can only start at backup end. The check would accept invalid targets in long backups and reject valid ones, and the last completed xid says little about commit order. He also noted that no consensus existed for the behaviour change, and returned the patch at the end of the CF.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
My point is that the
information you are working from (whatever checkpoint happens to be in
pg_control when recovery starts) is not sufficient for the task.  This
method is inaccurate and would disallow valid recovery scenarios.

precedents_retrieved.title: File level incremental backup
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Robert Haas, Fujii Masao, Bruce Momjian
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add file-level incremental backup to pg_basebackup: given the LSN or directory of a previous backup, send only data files containing blocks with an LSN newer than the threshold, and record a backup_profile file listing every file with its LSN, size and modification time. Reassembling a full backup from a base and an incremental backup was left to a separate restore tool, shown only as a Python prototype, with a C pg_restorebackup planned.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Committers did not accept the design: it reads every file even when nothing has changed and sends whole files when a single block has changed, so it offered little over timestamp-based tools and would leave file-level code to support after a block-level approach existed. Earlier feedback on avoiding the full read and on the backup profile had not been incorporated. The tool needed to reconstruct a usable backup was not part of the patch weeks after the final CommitFest deadline. Robert Haas proposed marking it Rejected, and Michael Paquier agreed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
At least 4 committers have looked at it and none of them are
convinced by the current design; feedback from almost half a year ago
hasn't been incorporated; obviously-needed parts of the patch
(pg_restorebackup) are missing weeks after the last CF deadline.

precedents_retrieved.title: [BUG] Panic due to incorrect missingContrecPtr after promotion
precedents_retrieved.summary: After a standby skipped a missing continuation record, missingContrecPtr stayed set, so on promotion the server wrote an overwrite_contrecord at a past LSN and later hit a WAL flush PANIC. The patch writes the overwrite_contrecord only when missingContrecPtr is ahead of the last WAL record, and adds a TAP test.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch was not committed because a separate commit, 6672d79, fixed the same issue. Robert Haas pointed to that commit, and the author confirmed it fixes the PANIC. Before that, Kyotaro Horiguchi's debugging of the author's logs suggested the inconsistent WAL came from the primary.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: For the benefit of anyone who may be looking at this thread in the archive later, I believe this commit will have fixed this issue:

precedents_retrieved.title: Be strict when request to flush past end of WAL in WaitXLogInsertionsToFinish
precedents_retrieved.summary: The thread first proposed raising the "request to flush past end of generated WAL" message in WaitXLogInsertionsToFinish() from LOG to PANIC. It later moved to a patch that makes XLogBackgroundFlush() honor the adjusted (clamped) return value instead of discarding it, plus a TAP test that reproduces the header-only flush that broke replay on a standby.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch was not rejected on its merits. Bharath Rupireddy created commitfest entry #7294 without knowing the author had already registered #7252 for the same thread. The author asked for #7294 to be withdrawn so the history stays in one entry, and it was withdrawn on the same day.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Could you withdraw #7294 so we don't split the history between two entries?

precedents_retrieved.title: Incorrect handling of OOM in WAL replay leading to data loss
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch set adds an error code (none, out-of-memory, invalid data) to the xlogreader error state, so callers can tell an OOM apart from an invalid record. The startup process then retries the record on OOM during crash recovery, so recovery does not end early and lose data.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew it. Commit 6b18b3fe2c2f had already made xlogreader.c fail harder on OOM, which leaves HEAD correct in the OOM cases. The patch set would have reverted that and made the xlogreader error layers more complicated, and nobody showed interest after a further commitfest.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I have been thinking about this patch for the last few days, and in light of 6b18b3fe2c2f I am going to withdraw it for now as this makes the error layers of the xlogreader more complicated.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Add redo LSN to pgstats files"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Add redo LSN to pgstats files"
Reverted commit(s): Add redo LSN to pgstats files
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit b860848232aa, that was added as a prerequisite for
the support of pgstats data flush across checkpoints, linking a pgstats
file to a specific checkpoint redo LSN.

As reported, this is proving to be currently problematic when going
through a pg_upgrade, that does direct manipulations of the control file
in the new cluster.  The LSN stored in the pgstats file is not able to
cope with any changes done in the control file by pg_upgrade yet,
causing the pgstats file to be discarded when starting the new cluster
after overriding its redo LSN (one is a `pg_resetwal -l` where the new
cluster's start LSN is bumped by a hardcoded value of 8 segments, see
copy_xact_xlog_xid).

The least painful path going forward is likely going to be a refactor of
the pgstats code so as it is possible to read and write some of its data
with some routines in src/common/, so as pg_upgrade or pg_resetwal are
able to update its data.  The main point is that we are going to need a
LSN in the stats file should we make it written at checkpoint time and
not only as part of a shutdown sequence.  It is too late to dive into
these details for v18, so let's revert the change, and let's try to
figure out all the details in the next release cycle.  The pgstats file
is currently only written as part of a shutdown sequence, and its
contents are still lost on crash, same as older releases.

Bump PGSTAT_FILE_FORMAT_ID.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: the corpus search returned no earlier attempt at the same or a similar idea. Inside the thread, message #6 links Ayush's and Sai Pranav's neighbouring fixes and Robert's original thread, but none of them is reported as a rejected attempt, and message #9 answers the 0003 question.

0003 changes what pg_available_wal_summaries() shows on a standby. Robert Haas says nothing relies on summaries ahead of replay (message #9), so I raise no compatibility objection about it. The patch adds no syntax, GUC or dumpable object.
The series adds no WAL record, catalog, or protocol change. 0003 narrows standby summarization to replay, and Robert Haas confirmed in message #9 that nothing relies on summaries ahead of replay.

The series has no privilege or exposure aspect. It changes internal WAL summarizer behaviour and an incremental backup check, adds no new privileges, roles, functions or settings, and does not change who can call pg_available_wal_summaries() or take backups.

The fit is sound otherwise. This is a correctness fix in core code, with no new GUC and no hot-path cost. Robert Haas, who knows this area, said in message #9 that nothing relies on standby summaries ahead of replay.

This is a bug fix for an assertion failure and for silent data loss in incremental backup after promotion. No existing feature, setting or extension avoids it. The fix changes the existing summarizer and incremental backup code and adds no second mechanism, so the already-implemented angle has nothing to object to.

This is a bug fix, not a feature, so the demand test does not apply in the usual way. The thread shows a cluster restart on cassert builds and silent wrong data from incremental backup on production builds since 17. Several people reproduced it independently, in messages #2, #3, #5, #7 and #12, and Robert Haas confirmed in message #9 that nothing relies on the old standby behaviour. The user group is everyone who uses summarize_wal and incremental backup with promotion, and no workaround is shown.
